_source_note: Draft checklist based on WHO/IMNCI (Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness) danger-sign framework. VERIFY every field against the official WHO/IMNCI document your team has selected before final use. Not a diagnostic tool.

age.description: Age of the patient (thresholds differ a lot for infants vs older children/adults)

duration.description: How long the fever/cold/diarrhoea has been present

temperature_or_how_hot.description: Measured temperature if available, or caregiver description of how high the fever feels

drinking_or_breastfeeding_ability.description: Whether the patient can drink/breastfeed normally, poorly, or not at all (IMNCI danger sign)

vomiting.description: Whether vomiting is present, and whether the patient vomits everything

convulsions.description: Any history of convulsions/fits during this illness (IMNCI danger sign)

lethargy_or_unconsciousness.description: Whether the patient is unusually sleepy, difficult to wake, or unconscious (IMNCI danger sign)

breathing_difficulty.description: Fast or difficult breathing, chest indrawing (relevant for cold/cough progressing to pneumonia)

blood_in_stool.description: For diarrhoea: whether there is blood in the stool (dysentery marker)

number_of_stools_per_day.description: For diarrhoea: frequency of loose stools

dehydration_signs.description: Sunken eyes, skin pinch goes back slowly, restlessness/irritability, reduced urination

cough_or_nasal_symptoms.description: For cold: presence of cough, runny/blocked nose, sore throat
